parts.label: i
parts.technique: Vector line equation, perpendicularity via scalar product
parts.reason: Uses vector equation of a line and dot product (OP·direction=0) to find perpendicular point; both vector line equation and dot product are explicitly listed as concepts no statement covers.

parts.label: ii
parts.technique: Finding position vector parallel to a given line's direction with fixed magnitude
parts.reason: Although finding a parallel vector with given magnitude is ordinary vector work (P10.2/P10.3, explicitly stated as IN in guidance), the vector here is derived from a line given via vector equation form l2: r=a+μb, which is the excluded 'vector equation of a line' concept. Borderline since only the direction vector is used.
